Graduate Application Instructions
Review admission requirements
Graduate applicants must have earned a four-year U.S. baccalaureate degree, or equivalent, from an accredited college or university, or complete the degree prior to enrollment.
Each graduate program may have its own additional admission requirements.
Review program-specific requirements
Qualified BGSU undergraduate students who are earning their bachelor’s degree may also be eligible to apply to a combined bachelor’s to master’s program. Review our list of programs with a combined bachelor’s to master’s pathway.
NOTE: If you plan to apply to more than one program, you must submit a separate application and application fee for each program.

Submit with your graduate application
Nonrefundable application fee
$45 for domestic applicants and $75 for international applicants
The application fee is automatically waived for:
McNair Scholars
U.S. military veterans
Returned Peace Corps volunteers,
K-12 public school teachers currently employed in the U.S.
Transcripts
For your application, submit unofficial transcripts from all institutions where you earned an undergraduate degree and from all institutions where you earned graduate-level credit. Upon admission, you will need to send final official or notarized copies of transcripts from all institutions where degrees were earned (showing dates when the degrees were conferred) and diplomas from international institutions. Evaluations by a NACES member organization are accepted. Current or previous BGSU students do not need to request a BGSU transcript. We will obtain it for you.
Standardized test scores
The Graduate College does not require GRE (Graduate Record Examination) scores for acceptance into graduate programs. However, test scores (GRE, GMAT, PRAXIS, OAE) may be required by the program. Review program-specific requirements.
BGSU code for GRE: 1069. For information on the GRE/GMAT/PRAXIS/TOEFL tests, visit the Educational Testing Service website.
Other documents
Your programs may also require recommendations, a statement of purpose, a resume and other documents. Review program-specific requirements
How to submit official transcripts and test scores
Mail to:
Graduate Admissions
200 University Hall

Bowling Green, OH 43403
Secure electronic transmission to:
gradapply@bgsu.edu
Are you an international student?
The application fee for international students is $75. We will not waive application fees.
Important note:
Review the admission requirements for international students. The page will explain:
How to submit necessary documents
Additional admission requirements, including English language proficiency requirements
Upon admission to the University you will receive further enrollment information from International Student Services in the International Programs and Partnerships Office.
Are you applying to physical or occupational therapy doctorate, or master’s in athletic training or speech-language pathology?
These programs require you to complete an application through a program-specific Centralized Application System (CAS). Consult your program for specific application directions.
Athletic training (MAT)
Communication disorders: speech-language pathology (M.S.)
Occupational therapy (OTD)
Physical therapy (DPT)
Some programs are not available to international students studying on an F-1 or J-1 student visa. Review our list of programs for international students.
Are you a graduate guest student?
A graduate guest student is a student who has earned a 4-year degree and who wishes to enroll in graduate or undergraduate courses without pursuing another degree.
There is no application fee.
You may take as many credits as you like as a guest student. However, if you decide to apply to a degree-granting program, you can transfer just 9 of those credit hours to a graduate program.
When submitting a graduate guest student application, please allow 4 business days for processing. Confirmation will be sent to your email address once the application has been processed.
International students who are considering taking graduate courses as a non-degree student should email the Office of International Programs and Partnerships for more information.
Applicants who have indicated a felony conviction will be notified within 1 business day if any additional information may be required.
